Q: Does an alias table need a primary key? Is the key just a composite of all the columns? A:

A combined unique key on game id + game name would make sense, if you want to prevent that you insert the same data twice. If the game ID for "The Settlers of Catan" is 37, and you already have a record 37 | Catan in your table - then you probably want to avoid inserting that exact same combination a second time.

Whether a unique index on just the game name would also make sense, depends on whether that should be unique across all games. If "The Settlers of Catan" already has the alias "Catan" - could there be a different game "Cats and Tigers acting mindlessly", that will also be published under the alias "Catan" ...? Don't know if that's a realistic scenario or not.

And the only queries for this table will be when I want to retrieve all names for a particular game id

Then an index on the game id column could also make sense, if you have a lot of data.

Q: What's the best way to learn Java in 2026 in your opinion? A:

Be aware of:

  • The Java language covers many fields, topics, many frameworks/libraries/modules.
  • The language has grown; there are many versions. Varying in syntax, constructs.
  • There are many magic frameworks (like lombok that generates getters/setters) and such.

This means be version aware in your field of work: what constructs, what products. Learn by programming, tutorials that might be dated. Blogs on subjects, for new things and specific topics.

Much programming. From time to time dive in the java language reference, and try things. Stackoverflow questions & answers. Blogs.

Notice the bloat of java, grown over time, happens in other successful languages like C++ too. (Or there is a backwards compatibility problem.) Java is a good solid and interesting choice.

Fine: I had very few courses, and paid, at the work place. University and such fine. Spending money, be careful: Courses for retraining/work agencies/other work orientation ("become a multimedia programmer"): I have my doubts.

Have unrelated interests like natural language translation or whatever an code stuff.
